The generalized modern river-region map retains the westward Euphrates, eastward Tigris, one shared lower channel and its contact with the Persian Gulf coast. Source meanders are simplified and locally separated; both named upstream rivers remain distinct until the single confluence at (127,164), and the common lower channel meets the coast at (135,179). This is a keyed modern physical baseline for Mesopotamia, not an ancient imperial border, calibrated river course or historical coastline.
